content.text:
I saved the heatmap as `/work/spec.vl.json`. It renders with no errors or warnings. Each column is a month (Feb 2018 – Dec 2025), each row is a depth (2 m at the top to 40 m at the bottom), and colour shows the monthly mean temperature. Months with no data for a depth are left blank: for example, 2 m in mid-2019 and mid-2024, 5 m in mid-2023, 40 m in late 2022 to early 2023, and 2 m in December 2025.

Main pattern: each summer the water at 2–5 m warms to about 16–18 °C. Water at 30–40 m stays much cooler and warms latest, in autumn. In winter all depths are at about 1–4 °C. Summer 2025 was clearly warmer at mid-depths (10–20 m) than earlier years.

```
REPORT
deliverable: spec.vl.json
requirements:
  R1: done - aggregate transform: mean of daily means per yearmonth × depth
  R2: done - temporal yearmonth x axis, Feb 2018–Dec 2025, one cell per month
  R3: done - months without data have no row after aggregation, so they show as blank cells
  R4: done - y axis labels each depth, ordinal sorted ascending 2→40 m
  R5: done - colour legend titled "Monthly mean temperature (°C)"
  R6: done - title plus a one-sentence caption (subtitle) stating the main pattern
assumptions:
  - Monthly mean = unweighted mean of the daily means (not weighted by n_obs)
  - A month counts as having data if at least one day has a valid mean temperature
  - Heatmap chosen over 7 lines so that gaps show clearly
limitations:
  - Months with only a few days of data look the same as full months; the day count is shown only in the tooltip
  - The temperature ranges in the caption were read from the data during development; they are static text, not computed by the spec
  - The "blank = no data" note is in the x-axis title so the caption stays one sentence
```
